title: Parking Lot System
summary: Design a parking lot that supports multiple vehicle types (motorcycle, car, bus), multiple floors, and computes parking fees.
requirements: Support multiple vehicle types with different spot size requirements
Support multiple floors, each with a limited number of spots per type
Assign the nearest available suitable spot when a vehicle enters
Track entry and exit time and compute a parking fee on exit
Handle the lot being full gracefully
hints: Think about whether Spot should know its own type or whether that lives elsewhere
How would you add a new vehicle type without touching existing spot logic?

title: Elevator Control System
summary: Design the control logic for a bank of elevators in a building, handling internal and external requests efficiently.
requirements: Support multiple elevators serving the same set of floors
Handle external up/down requests and internal floor requests
Decide which elevator should service a new request
Support an elevator going out of service
Avoid starving requests at floors far from current elevator positions
hints: Separate 'scheduling which elevator responds' from 'how one elevator moves'
Consider representing elevator state explicitly (idle/moving up/moving down/door open)

title: Vending Machine
summary: Design a vending machine that accepts coins/notes, lets a user select an item, dispenses it, and returns change.
requirements: Track inventory and price per item slot
Accept incremental payment and track balance
Reject selection if item is out of stock or payment is insufficient
Dispense the item and correct change
Support restocking and refunding on cancel
hints: This is a good problem for practicing an explicit state machine (Idle/HasMoney/Dispensing)

title: API Rate Limiter
summary: Design an in-process rate limiter that can be attached to an API to limit requests per client per time window.
requirements: Support a configurable limit per client within a time window
Support at least two different limiting algorithms (e.g. fixed window and sliding window)
Allow switching the algorithm without changing calling code
Be safe under concurrent access from multiple threads/requests
Expose whether a given request should be allowed or rejected
hints: This is a strong candidate for a Strategy interface with swappable algorithm implementations

title: Library Management System
summary: Design a system to manage books, members, and borrowing/returning with due dates and fines.
requirements: Track book copies and their availability
Let a member borrow a book if a copy is available and they have no unpaid fines
Compute a fine when a book is returned late
Support reserving a book that is currently unavailable
Support multiple copies of the same title
hints: Think about the difference between a Book (the title) and a BookCopy (a physical item)
